title.narrative: Enhancing cassava production and diversified utilization for food and incomes in Rwanda_Gwiza Muhinzi

description.narrative: The proposed project seeks to (1) increase access to key production inputs for cassava farming i.e., quality seed of the recently released improved varieties for smallholder farmers, particularly women, (2) promote better agronomy for cassava through practical trainings and approaches to deliver proven technologies such as the Zai Pit technique promoted by INGABO and partners among other practices, (3) improve quality and safety of dried roots through piloting with industry players post-harvest handling and storage (PHHS) technologies that fit local farmers¿ contexts, (4) expand income generating opportunities for value chain actors, particularly women and youth, through piloting with local market players proven innovations that enhance diversified utilization of cassava roots and peels (HQCF for baking and other foods and HQCP for animal feed), and (5) advocate for more uptake of innovations and good practices along the cassava value chains, greater investment in, and a better coordinated sub-sector using what will have been documented as evidence for what works. This will benefit smallholder farmers, particularly women, to achieve better yields through (1) and (2), improved food quality and safety through (3), improved incomes and jobs for actors particularly women and youth through (4), and a better functioning sub-sector in general through (5).

comment.narrative: Output 1.2The new NRMV including government response to other types of abuse and crimesother than trafficking in persons is piloted.

In March 2022 the Moldovan Government approved the program to create and develop a National Referral Mechanism for the Protection and Assistance of Victims of Crimes of the Republic of Moldova for 20222026 NRMV Program which is meant to gradually replace the National Referral System for Assistance of Victims and potential victims of trafficking. The new NRMV managed by MLSP is designed to assist all victims of violent crimes including victims of trafficking and genderbased violence. Since the beginning of the refugee crisis in the Republic of Moldova the MLSP declared that the refugees and thirdcountry nationals TCNs victims of crime can access the support available under the NRMV. With the support of FPI IOM provided technical and expert support to the MLSP to pilot the newly adopted program.
